sections.title: A diverse genus
sections.text: Ranunculus includes many annual and perennial herbs; size and leaf form vary widely by species. This plate resembles a yellow-flowered buttercup with deeply divided basal leaves, but its genus-level label does not allow a secure species identification or a reliable size estimate.

sections.title: Irritation and toxicity
sections.text: Many buttercups contain ranunculin, which can release the irritant protoanemonin when fresh tissue is crushed. Fresh plants can irritate skin and mucous membranes and should not be eaten; toxicity varies among species and plant parts. Kew specifically advises against fresh or home-prepared medicinal use of meadow buttercup.

sections.title: Image details
sections.text: The illustration's glossy yellow flowers and divided leaves are consistent with a buttercup, but do not prove a particular species.
